A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multiscale GNN training framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and split tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification, ShapeNet segmentation, PPI and Qtips experiments, including accuracy, computational-cost and timing results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds OGBN-MAG, MNIST-derived graph and held-out Qtips results, together with a training-loss comparison.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same coarsening, parameter transfer and telescoping loss procedures. The new theoretical analysis and additional tested connectivity settings do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds MNIST pixel-graph node labeling and evaluation on OGBN-MAG's homogeneous paper-citation graph, substantially extending the evaluated data coverage. Qtips was already used in v1; its additional results do not constitute a newly introduced dataset or task.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain fine-grid training and the same random, Topk, subgraph and hybrid alternatives. The added evaluations reuse existing comparison approaches. FastGCN is newly cited but is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix B experiments introduce held-out Qtips evaluation with 100 training and 1,000 test rods, a 500-epoch baseline and a [400,200,100] multiscale schedule. MNIST uses 1,000 training and 100 test graphs, and the new sweeps include p=3. Retained benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an OGBN-Arxiv convergence comparison in Figure 5 and extends pooling/connectivity analyses through Qtips and MNIST classification experiments, including p=3. These extend the existing diagnostics; the original Qtips loss-discrepancy analysis in Table 1 is unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing three-seed and standard-deviation reporting is retained. Added result tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting format; no increased run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark values are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results. Table 4 reports OGBN-MAG accuracy of 37.07% for four-level random coarsening versus 35.73% for fine-grid training. Tables 6–7 report best multiscale Qtips/MNIST scores of 73.30%/86.04%, versus respective baselines of 73.03%/86.28%. Figure 5 adds convergence trajectories.

T1.justification: v3 introduces linear-model and sketching definitions, embedding assumptions, Theorem 4.1 and its Appendix A proof with residual analysis. These are absent from v1. Section 5 also removes the separate explicit GIN and GAT computational-cost formulas while retaining the GCN formula.

C1.justification: The abstract newly identifies theoretical analysis as a contribution. The three training strategies and the principal claims about efficiency, predictive performance and broad applicability remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds an interpretation connecting approximation quality to omitted edges and the residual. Section 4.4 softens the categorical statement about loss variance without enhanced connectivity, and Section 6.1 acknowledges that more advanced architectures could outperform the OGBN-MAG GCN baseline.

D1.justification: v3 documents additional experimental details, including 256-channel GCNs, Qtips training budgets, MNIST pixel-to-node and spatial-kNN construction, and OGBN-MAG paper/citation extraction. Existing setup tables remain substantively unchanged, although some restyled timing/FLOP captions omit earlier coarsening-level qualifiers.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to FastGCN, LeCun et al.'s MNIST-related work and Woodruff's sketching treatment. Sketching provides a new theoretical connection, while the existing related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, the author list changes, and several explanations and transitions are edited. The Planetoid discussion moves to Appendix D and appendix organization improves, but most existing methodological prose and the conclusion remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 extensively reformats and relocates tables, including splitting v1 Table 6 into Tables 9–10. It merges the random/Topk illustrations, wraps text around the subgraph illustration, and adds a gradient-computation diagram, a convergence plot and new result tables. Captions, headers and highlighting also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful empirical coverage, held-out Qtips tests, a convergence diagnostic and clearer tables. However, its newly advertised theoretical contribution introduces a substantive proof gap: Appendix A, Equation (18), bounds a squared norm of a sum by the sum of squared norms without controlling the cross term. These empirical and presentation gains coexist with a new theoretical reliability problem, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
